stories.label: Oil tops $110 as Houthi drone strike near Saudi Shaybah field rattles markets | The National
stories.summary: New development: a Houthi drone struck near Saudi Aramco's Shaybah oilfield in the Empty Quarter, and Brent crude extended above $110 a barrel. Lead with the mechanism: the East-West pipeline to Yanbu was Saudi Arabia's way around a closed Hormuz, and repeated hits on it and now Shaybah are putting a risk premium on the bypass routes too. Say who pays (importers in India and the Philippines, named in the coverage). Name Brent crude. Dateline Shaybah.

stories.label: US orders some diplomats to leave Saudi Arabia amid Houthi threat
stories.summary: Decision, not rhetoric: the State Department ordered non-emergency staff and families out of its Saudi mission, saying the Houthis have 'increasingly engaged in hostilities' against the kingdom, while denying a wider Gulf withdrawal (The National). Lead with what the order signals about how far the Iran war has spread onto Saudi soil, days after Macron's surprise Riyadh visit, and who stays exposed: the millions of migrant workers who have no evacuation order. Dateline Riyadh.

stories.label: Zelensky calls for 'freezing front' to end war
stories.summary: New development after Witkoff's Moscow trip: Putin agreed to resume US-mediated talks with Ukraine as soon as November, and Zelensky publicly called for freezing the front line as the first step to a ceasefire. Lead with the shift: Kyiv now proposing to stop where the lines are, which concedes occupied land de facto for now. Note Russian missile strikes on Kyiv continued (France 24). Dateline Kyiv.

stories.label: Ukraine's anti-corruption agencies search National Bank premises
stories.summary: NABU and SAPO detectives searched the National Bank of Ukraine and the governor's premises: a corruption probe that has already reached the state nuclear monopoly Energoatom, the president's former chief of staff and the prosecutor general's office now touches the central bank that holds the reserves and Western aid flows. Lead with that reach, say exactly what the investigators are looking at and what the bank says, and why it matters for donors as peace talks restart. Do not use Zero Hedge's speculation. Dateline Kyiv.

stories.label: Long-End US Yield Hits One-Month Low as AI Fears Fuel Haven Bid
stories.summary: Tesla's and Meta's outlooks revived doubts that AI spending will pay, Asian equities fell, and money ran to Treasuries: long-end yields hit a one-month low even with oil above $110, which would normally push them up. Lead with that tension — a war-driven oil shock and an AI-driven flight to safety pulling the US 10-year Treasury yield in opposite directions — and say what lower yields mean for borrowers such as Pakistan (Dawn). Name the US 10-year Treasury yield. Dateline New York.

stories.label: eMudhra breach: eMudhra breach: Netizens react as IT Ministry says impact on Indian sites 'very limited'
stories.summary: eMudhra, a licensed certifying authority that issues India's digital signatures and TLS certificates, disclosed that the private keys for eight of its intermediate certificates were compromised. Lead with the mechanism: whoever holds those keys can mint certificates browsers trust, so Mozilla, Google and Apple must decide whether to distrust the chain, while the IT Ministry calls the impact 'very limited'. Say what was signed, who revoked what, and what it means for India's e-sign and government sites. Dateline Bengaluru.

stories.label: Muse刚火，小扎就催它挣钱了
stories.summary: Meta posted record revenue but its free cash flow turned negative as AI capital spending outran income, and Zuckerberg is now pressing its new Muse model to earn money sooner. Lead with the negative free cash flow: the clearest sign yet of what the AI build-out costs, and the reason markets sold off overnight. Use the Chinese tech press's reading of the numbers. Dateline Menlo Park.

stories.label: 英伟达投的AI语音独角兽发两款新模型，半秒内就能实时响应，附实测
stories.summary: ElevenLabs released Eleven Realtime Mini and Max, voice-agent models that answer in about 0.57 seconds, yet on Artificial Analysis's Big Bench Audio voice-reasoning test Max (98.8%) ranks third behind two Chinese models, StepFun's StepAudio 3 Realtime (99.7%) and Alibaba's Qwen Audio 3.0 Realtime Plus (99.2%). Lead with that ranking, explain the cascaded design (speech recognition, LLM, speech synthesis) and its trade-off, and give the prices. Zhidx's hands-on test found a strong foreign accent in Chinese. Dateline London.

stories.label: La comisión de Bukele decide “a puertas cerradas” quién sale de las cárceles del régimen
stories.summary: After more than four years of El Salvador's state of exception, in which the government insists only gang members are jailed, a government commission decides behind closed doors which detainees are released, with no public criteria, no court and no appeal. Lead with the opacity: the same state that arrested tens of thousands without trial now frees some without explanation, which admits wrongful detentions without naming or compensating them. Give the figures Focos reports. Dateline San Salvador.

stories.label: Bet Blaze funcionou em endereço de empresas ligadas a Willer Tomaz, investigado pela PF
stories.summary: Agência Pública found that the betting site Blaze operated from the address of companies linked to Willer Tomaz, a lawyer close to Senator Flávio Bolsonaro who is suing Blaze for R$163 million he says he bet, and whom the Federal Police are investigating for money laundering. Lead with the address: the man suing the platform appears tied to its own operation. Explain why Brazil's online betting boom has become a laundering channel, and the election-season stakes. Dateline Brasília.

stories.label: Baby manta rays hunker down close to coasts before facing the open ocean's dangers
stories.summary: New research finds giant manta ray pups spend their first years in shallow coastal nurseries before moving into the open ocean, where sharks and orcas hunt them. Lead with the finding and what it means for protection: an endangered species that breeds slowly depends on coastal waters that fishing, development and bycatch hit hardest. Name the study, the site and the method. Dateline from where the study was done.

stories.label: France's Macron says protesters won't be allowed to 'cause chaos'
stories.summary: New since our bond-yield story: Macron accuses foreign leaders, Trump among them, of exploiting France's riots for their own elections after they blamed Muslim migrants for the violence. Lead with the attribution fight: who is being blamed for student-led unrest over school funding and rents, and what that does to France's Muslim citizens. Say what the protesters are demanding and what the state has done (curfews, Paris protest ban). Dateline Paris.

stories.label: 'No enriched nuclear material will leave Iran': Tehran tells Pakistan army chief Asim Munir amid US peace deal deadlock
stories.summary: Iran told Pakistan's army chief Asim Munir, who is carrying mediators' proposals, that no enriched uranium will leave the country, the sticking point in any deal to end the US-Israeli war on Iran. Lead with the red line and the mediator: a Muslim nuclear power's general shuttling between Washington and Tehran. Add that top security official Mohsen Rezaei told Drop Site Iran expects a US-Israeli strike before the US midterms and has new targets, and that Russia offers to mediate (TASS, label it). Dateline Tehran.

stories.label: How Qatar, Turkiye, Pakistan and Indonesia are deepening defence ties
stories.summary: Qatar, Turkiye, Pakistan and Indonesia signed a defence-industry cooperation accord on Wednesday, a separate deal from the Mecca pact Turkiye sent to parliament this week. Lead with who is in it: the Muslim world's most populous state, its only nuclear power, a NATO member and the Gulf's richest per head. Mechanism: joint production of drones, ships and munitions so members buy less from the US and Europe; say what the accord commits and note India's reading of it (Times of India). Dateline Ankara.

stories.label: Russia ready to resume trilateral Ukraine talks in November: Kremlin
stories.summary: New development after Witkoff's Moscow visit: Putin told the US envoy Russia will return to US-mediated talks with Ukraine around 10 November, possibly in Abu Dhabi. Lead with the date and venue. Both sources are state media (TRT World, TASS): attribute the claim to the Kremlin as reported, do not state it as fact. Mechanism: Washington holds the leverage (the strike-warning intelligence it switched off and on), and a Gulf state hosts. Dateline Moscow.

stories.label: Políticos têm rede ‘paralela’ na Meta sem declarar ao TSE
stories.summary: Days before Brazil's tied runoff, Agência Pública found politicians running undeclared 'parallel' support networks on Meta's platforms, hidden from the electoral court (TSE): Flávio Bolsonaro has more than seven undeclared support profiles, and André Janones, Campopiano and Pavanato have them too. Lead with the count. Mechanism: Brazilian law requires campaigns to declare the accounts they use, so undeclared pages escape spending and content rules. Dateline Brasília.

stories.label: Colombia president removes artefacts from National Museum in ‘cultural counter-revolution’
stories.summary: Colombia's new president Abelardo de la Espriella has ordered artefacts removed from the National Museum as part of a declared 'fight against wokism'. Lead with what was removed and whose history it represented (Indigenous, Afro-Colombian, the armed conflict's victims). Mechanism: executive control of national memory institutions; say who decides, what law covers it, and who objects. Dateline Bogotá.

stories.label: Meta fined $25 billion in New Mexico over Cambridge Analytica scandal
stories.summary: A New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay $25 billion for deceiving Facebook users about privacy, a month after the company was found liable over the Cambridge Analytica breach before the 2016 election. Lead with the number and that a single state did it a decade on. Mechanism: state consumer-protection law, which counts violations per user, can produce penalties larger than federal regulators ever imposed (the FTC's $5 billion in 2019). Say whether Meta will appeal. Dateline Santa Fe.

stories.label: Tesla profits drop 43% in Q3
stories.summary: Tesla's third-quarter profit fell 43% and its energy-storage business shrank, on the same day reports said SpaceX and Tesla are exploring a merger that would combine about 30,000 bitcoin on their books (CoinDesk). Lead with the profit fall. Mechanism: fewer cars sold than a year earlier, price cuts and capital spending on AI; the merger would fold a shrinking carmaker into a rocket company fresh from a blowout quarter. Dateline Austin.

stories.label: Opposition calls Godongwana's fuel levy cuts 'a scam' as GNU offers muted support
stories.summary: South Africa's finance minister Enoch Godongwana cut the fuel levy in his medium-term budget, and the opposition calls it electioneering. Lead with the size of the cut and what it saves a household at the pump, then what the Treasury gives up and how it plans to cover it. Mechanism: oil above $110 (Brent crude) passes straight into South African fuel prices, so the levy is the one lever the state controls. Dateline Cape Town.

stories.label: Govt reduces petrol price by Rs2.71 per litre, ups high-speed diesel rate by Re0.31
stories.summary: New decision since our petroleum-levy protest story: Pakistan cut petrol by Rs2.71 a litre and raised high-speed diesel by Rs0.31 for the next fortnight. Lead with the split: petrol is what motorcycles and cars burn, diesel moves goods, buses and tractors, so the rise lands on freight and food prices. Mechanism: the fortnightly price set from import costs plus the petroleum levy the IMF programme requires; tie to Brent crude. Dateline Islamabad.

stories.label: Japanese visitors could soon pay with yen stablecoins in South Korea under Shinhan-SBI pact
stories.summary: South Korea's Shinhan Card and Japan's SBI have tested letting Japanese visitors pay in Korea with yen stablecoins linked to payment cards. Lead with what it bypasses: the currency exchange and card-network fees on cross-border spending. Mechanism: a regulated yen-pegged token settling across a border, which Japan licensed and Korea has not yet; say it has no commercial timeline. Name the yen. Dateline Seoul.

stories.label: 腾讯内部的“AI搜索配方”，公开了！
stories.summary: Tencent has opened its Yuanbao search engine, which already handles hundreds of millions of calls a day inside 50 Tencent products, to outside developers as an API, MCP server and Skill on Tencent Cloud. Lead with the engineering numbers: a hundred-billion-page index, recall up from under 80% to over 93%, and servers cut from 3,200 to 400. Mechanism: AI agents need live search to avoid stale answers; OpenAI and Google bundle it into their models, Tencent sells it separately so developers can use any model (Zhidx tested it with DeepSeek). Dateline Shenzhen.

stories.label: Ghost Shark Uncrewed Submarine Shown Launching Aerial Drones For The First Time
stories.summary: New video shows Australia's Ghost Shark, the extra-large uncrewed submarine Anduril builds for the Royal Australian Navy, launching aerial drones from a 12-tube launcher for the first time. Lead with the capability: a crewless sub that can surface sensors and strike drones far from any ship. Mechanism: Australia's bet on cheap autonomous undersea craft while its AUKUS nuclear submarines are a decade or more away. Dateline Sydney.

stories.label: Airbus Ships First Lightweight Vulcain Aft Bay for Ariane 6 Block 2
stories.summary: Airbus Netherlands has delivered the first lightweight engine bay for Ariane 6's Block 2 upgrade, but the weight saved is smaller than first planned. Lead with the shortfall in kilograms. Mechanism: every kilogram cut from the core stage becomes payload, and Block 2 is Europe's answer to SpaceX on price for launching its own satellites; say what the smaller saving means for Block 2's payload target. Dateline Leiden.

stories.label: Study finds air quality warnings had only a modest impact on Montrealers' movements during wildfires
stories.summary: A McGill study in Health & Place used city travel data to show that federal warnings to stay indoors during Canada's worst wildfire-smoke episodes changed Montrealers' movements far less than health officials hoped. Lead with the size of the drop. Mechanism: who could not stay home (shift workers, people without cooled indoor space) and why advisories alone do not protect them as smoke seasons grow. Dateline Montreal.

stories.label: US congressional candidate Brad Lander freed after West Bank detention
stories.summary: Israeli forces detained a US congressional candidate and dozens of volunteers who were helping Palestinian farmers harvest their olives; Lander was released with a warning, but he says dozens remain in custody. Lead with who is still held and what they were doing, not with the American: the harvest is when West Bank farmers lose access to their own groves, and the volunteers were there because settlers and soldiers block it. Mechanism: Israeli military orders that make a harvest on your own land a security matter. Dateline the village where they were detained.

stories.label: France's Macron arrives in Saudi Arabia for unscheduled visit during Gulf tour
stories.summary: New development since our 10-20 story on Macron's UAE and Bahrain diesel deal: he flew unannounced to Riyadh, the first Western leader to land in Saudi Arabia since Houthi attacks reached the kingdom, and met Mohammed bin Salman on energy and security. Lead with the 'solidarity' visit as a trade: a French president under cost-of-living protests at home buying Gulf fuel by standing beside a crown prince under fire. Say what, if anything, was agreed on diesel; name Brent crude. Dateline Riyadh.

stories.label: Diesel diplomacy: The American rush for black gold
stories.summary: Russia is sending its first diesel tanker to the United States under Trump's deal with Putin to bring down US diesel prices, yet Ukraine's drone swarms have crippled the refineries of the world's second-largest diesel exporter, and analysts told Reuters Russia may not have the fuel to deliver. Lead with the contradiction: Washington is buying fuel from the refineries Kyiv is burning, while sanctions on Russian oil still stand for everyone else. Name Brent crude. Dateline Moscow.

stories.label: UN issues call to arms to combat 'off the charts' El Niño
stories.summary: The World Meteorological Organization says the El Niño now forming could be the strongest on record. Lead with the measurement, the Pacific sea-surface anomaly and how it compares with 1997-98 and 2015-16, not with tabloid 'mega-floods'. Mechanism: how a warm Pacific shifts rainfall, so the cost falls on monsoon farmers in Pakistan, Indonesia and southern Africa, and on food prices; name wheat. Use the Dawn source for the South Asian outlook. Dateline Geneva.

stories.label: Thousands march across Greece over school funding and rents
stories.summary: More than 10,000 students, teachers, parents and unions marched in Athens and Thessaloniki over crumbling schools, teacher shortages and rents students cannot pay. Lead with the demands and the numbers, not the 'Europe boils over' framing; then place it beside the cost-of-living unrest in France and Italy and name what the three share. TRT World is Turkish state media: prefer any Greek or wire detail the writer can find, and attribute claims accordingly. Dateline Athens.

stories.label: LHC moved for release of Imran's sisters as 30-day detention period ends
stories.summary: All three of jailed former prime minister Imran Khan's sisters, Aleema Khan, Noreen Niazi and Uzma Khan, have been held for 30 days under detention orders, and Aleema's son has petitioned the Lahore High Court for their release. Lead with three women detained without charge for their brother's politics. Mechanism: preventive-detention law that lets the provincial government hold people without trial and renew the order; say on what grounds they were held and whether the order can be extended. Dateline Lahore.

stories.label: Hospitals in Gaza face power shutdowns; U.S. polling firm admits fabricating data; Water crisis in Yemen
stories.summary: Write only the lead item of this digest: Gaza's remaining hospitals face power shutdowns. Lead with which hospitals, how many patients depend on power (incubators, dialysis, ICU) and how many hours of fuel are left. Mechanism: Israel's control of fuel entry, which decides whether generators run; name who holds the fuel and what has been let in. Ignore the polling and Yemen items. Dateline Gaza City or the hospital's city.

stories.label: Egypt Forum 2026 celebrates higher attendance at schools still struggling without teachers or classrooms
stories.summary: Egypt's government celebrated higher school attendance at its Egypt Forum while schools still lack teachers and classrooms. Lead with the gap between the official figure and the classroom: the teacher shortfall, class sizes, and education spending against the constitutional minimum. Name Education Minister Mohamed Abdel Latif and the weekly-assessment rule that drew parliamentary pushback. Dateline Cairo.

stories.label: Saudi crude oil exports hit five-month high in August, data shows
stories.summary: Saudi crude exports rose 7.9% in August to 4.45 million barrels a day, a five-month high, even as production fell to a record low of 6.24 million. Lead with the paradox: the kingdom pumped less than ever but shipped more, so it drew on stocks and burned less at home. Mechanism: with Hormuz mined, how much moves west through the East-West pipeline to Yanbu on the Red Sea, now itself under Houthi fire. Name Brent crude and ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb. Dateline Riyadh.

stories.label: Without USAID, Guatemala’s Maya reserve must support itself
stories.summary: The end of USAID funding has left the community forest concessions of Guatemala's Maya Biosphere Reserve, long held up as proof that locals protect forest better than parks do, to pay for patrols and fire crews themselves. Lead with the dollar gap and what it funded. Mechanism: timber and non-timber income that must now cover what aid paid, against cattle ranching and trafficking pressure. Dateline Flores or the nearest town named.

stories.label: Does opting out of smart TV tracking work? Research finds "suspicious" traffic.
stories.summary: Researchers found smart TVs running Samsung's Tizen, Vizio and Roku keep sending data to automatic content recognition endpoints after the owner opts out. Lead with the opt-out that does not stop the traffic. Mechanism: ACR fingerprints whatever is on screen, including from HDMI inputs, and sells viewing profiles to advertisers; say what the research measured and what the makers answered. Dateline where the researchers are based.

stories.label: The $15 billion ad-powered AI startup your doctor may already be using
stories.summary: Nearly two-thirds of US doctors now consult OpenEvidence, an AI search engine paid for by pharmaceutical advertising and valued at $15 billion. Lead with the business model: the tool that answers a doctor's treatment question is funded by companies selling the treatments. Mechanism: drug ads beside clinical answers, outside the rules that govern drug marketing to physicians; say what is known about its accuracy. Dateline Miami.

stories.label: Cops Warned to Look for ‘Suspicious Behavior’ From People Opposing Flock at City Council Meetings
stories.summary: A police surveillance document obtained by 404 Media tells officers to watch for 'suspicious behavior' and 'emotional confrontations' from residents who speak against Flock licence-plate cameras at city council meetings. Lead with public comment being treated as a threat. Name who wrote the document, who received it, and how many towns have voted to drop Flock. Dateline the city of the issuing agency.

stories.label: LKA Baden-Württemberg: Kritik an Gesichtserkennung bei Demo-Teilnehmenden
stories.summary: A Baden-Württemberg state police officer investigating Palestine activists allegedly ran facial recognition on uninvolved people who had attended the same demonstration; the civil-rights group Gesellschaft für Freiheitsrechte calls it unlawful, 'investigating into the blue'. Lead with bystanders identified for attending a protest. Mechanism: the federal photo database and the legal threshold for matching faces, and how pro-Palestine protest in Germany became a reason to lower it. Dateline Stuttgart.

stories.label: Scientists discover migration-mediated mechanism enabling bacteria-virus coexistence
stories.summary: Researchers at the University of Maryland and the University of Exeter show that bacteria and the viruses that infect them can coexist through migration between patches, not only through the evolutionary arms race long assumed. Lead with the overturned assumption. Then say why it matters: phage therapy against antibiotic-resistant infections depends on predicting when phages wipe out bacteria and when they settle into coexistence. Name the journal. Dateline College Park.

stories.label: Governments Take Websites Offline After PHP Security Warnings
stories.summary: Finland took every public-facing government service offline and Dutch national and local bodies followed, after warnings about critical flaws in PHP — the language under up to 70% of the world's websites, WordPress included. WSJ reports an AI system found the bug. Lead with a state pulling its whole web presence as a precaution; the mechanism is one language that much of the internet depends on, and the question of who patches the long tail of sites nobody maintains.

stories.label: Armenia could lose more than half of remittances from Russia
stories.summary: A Eurasian Economic Union report warns Armenia could lose more than half its remittances from Russia if it keeps moving toward the EU, and Foreign Minister Mirzoyan says Yerevan is still drafting its answer. Lead with the size of the remittance dependence: the mechanism is how a migrant-labour economy is tied to a bloc it wants to leave, and who pays — Armenian households, not the government. Azerbaijani and Russian state coverage frame it differently; use the contrast.

stories.label: Poland Blasts Ukrainian City's Honor for World War II Fighters
stories.summary: Lviv's council dedicated 2027 to the Ukrainian Insurgent Army and figures like Roman Shukhevych, whose units massacred Poles in Volhynia, and Tusk called it 'harmful for Ukraine.' Lead with the rift opening between Kyiv and its most important logistics ally while Ukraine's peace talks and EU bid are in play; the mechanism is how unresolved wartime memory becomes leverage in Polish politics.

stories.label: 'Where are the courts?': Killing of Multan suspect in alleged CCD encounter sparks concern among lawyers, journalists
stories.summary: A suspect in Multan died in what Punjab's Crime Control Department calls an exchange of fire, the latest of the 'encounter' killings rights groups have tied to the CCD since it was set up last year. Name the institution and the provincial government that created it; lead with the lawyers' question — 'where are the courts?' — and the mechanism: a police unit that skips trial, with a count of its encounter deaths if the source gives one.

stories.label: JI announces third wave of anti-levy protests across country on Friday
stories.summary: Jamaat-i-Islami is calling sit-ins in every district of Pakistan on Friday against the petroleum levy, as Brent crude tops $110 on the Gulf war. Lead with what the levy adds per litre and who pays it; the mechanism is an IMF-programme government taxing fuel for revenue at the moment a war has already pushed the import bill up. Name Brent crude as the series.

stories.label: Revealed: Expensive gas behind ‘nearly 90%’ of rise in UK electricity bills
stories.summary: Carbon Brief's analysis finds wholesale gas costs explain nearly 90% of the rise in UK household electricity bills, not green levies. Lead with the 90%; the mechanism is marginal pricing, where gas sets the power price even when most supply is cheaper, so a Hormuz-driven gas spike lands on every bill. Name natural gas prices as the series, and tie it to the Bank of England's expected hike on energy-driven inflation.

stories.label: Hong Kong working to boost global banks' use of yuan trading tools
stories.summary: Hong Kong is recruiting foreign banks into its Central Moneymarkets Unit, the bond-clearing system, to make the city the main offshore yuan hub. Lead with the plumbing: clearing is what makes a currency usable outside the dollar system, and the push comes as sanctions and war raise the cost of dollar dependence. Name the yuan as the series.

stories.label: CSTO to supply weapons to Tajikistan to strengthen border with Afghanistan
stories.summary: Russian state agency TASS reports the Russia-led CSTO will begin arms deliveries to Tajikistan to fortify its 1,300km border with Taliban-ruled Afghanistan; the CSTO chief insists it threatens no one. State-media only: attribute every claim to TASS. Lead with Moscow arming a Central Asian frontier while it fights in Ukraine; the mechanism is Russia keeping its security umbrella over Central Asia as China and the Taliban shift the region.

stories.label: Ebola: Nigerian lawmakers demand release of outstanding funds for health agencies to strengthen response
stories.summary: New development on the Abuja Ebola case: Nigeria's House of Representatives says money already appropriated for health agencies has not been released, and demands it now for surveillance and contact tracing. Lead with the gap between budgeted and disbursed funds while the virus is in the capital; the accountability point is that the executive holds money parliament voted for outbreak response.

stories.label: Europe weighs giving utilities, infrastructure companies more powers to bring down drones
stories.summary: European officials are weighing letting power utilities and other infrastructure operators shoot down or jam drones themselves, fearing strikes like Russia's on Ukraine's grid could black out millions. Lead with private companies gaining a use-of-force power once reserved for militaries and police; the question is who is accountable when a utility brings down the wrong aircraft.

stories.label: Someone Opened a CashApp In Her Name. She Faces Years in Prison
stories.summary: Amanda Smith spent three nights in jail and faces years in prison because a Facebook Marketplace scam produced a CashApp account in her name, which she says she never opened. Lead with her; the mechanism is prosecutors treating account records from a fintech's weak identity checks as proof of who did it, so the cost of the platform's lax KYC lands on the person whose identity was stolen.

stories.label: The Chestnut Grove Caught in the Middle of A Years-Long Data Center Fight
stories.summary: A grove of rare surviving American chestnuts — a species blight all but wiped out — sits in the path of an AI data center in West Virginia, and locals have fought it for years. Lead with the trees as the concrete cost; the mechanism is how the AI build-out takes land, power and water through state incentives that leave local communities little say.

stories.label: DeepSeek Wants Better AI at Lower Cost
stories.summary: DeepSeek shipped a V4.1 Flash update built to finish tasks faster with shorter outputs, and open-sourced a framework for cheaper inference. Lead with the cost of running a model, not training it: the Chinese labs are competing on inference efficiency under US chip export controls, and an open framework hands that saving to every rival. Give the speed or cost figures the source reports.

stories.label: Drone attack in disputed Sudan-South Sudan border region kills at least 153
stories.summary: A drone hit a market in Abyei, the oil-rich border region both Sudans claim, killing at least 153; South Sudanese officials blame Sudan's army, and MSF is treating burn victims. New development on yesterday's unattributed '160 killed' roundup: this one has a place, a named accused attacker and a toll. Lead with the market and the toll; the mechanism is how the SAF–RSF war's drone campaign now spills into a UN-patrolled disputed zone with no functioning administration.

stories.label: Russia frees U.S. citizen held since 2022, state media reports
stories.summary: Material new development in the Ukraine-talks arc: a day after Trump said he raised Stephen Hubbard with Putin, Russia released the American, convicted as a 'mercenary', while Witkoff was in Moscow. Lead with the release and its timing; the mechanism is prisoners as currency in the US–Russia channel that is running alongside, and around, Kyiv. Kyiv Independent ties it to the Witkoff visit.

stories.label: Emissions Gap Report Identifies U.S. as Outlier Among G20 Nations
stories.summary: UNEP's annual Emissions Gap Report says current policies point to about 2.8C of warming this century, that a 1.5C overshoot is now inevitable, and singles out the United States as the G20 outlier whose abandoned pledge raised the odds. Lead with the 2.8C figure and the US as the named cause; who pays is the Global South (Hindustan Times carries the Indian framing). Carbon Brief has the report's figures.

stories.label: Departamento de imigração dos EUA diz que Ramagem é imigrante ilegal e violou leis
stories.summary: The US Department of Homeland Security says Alexandre Ramagem, Bolsonaro's former intelligence (Abin) chief who fled Brazil as a fugitive, is in the US illegally and broke its laws, and could be deported or detained. Lead with the DHS statement; the mechanism is whether Washington, which has backed Bolsonaro's camp, hands back a convicted ally days before a tied runoff. Brazil-runoff arc.

stories.label: Australian lawmaker loses both legs in vehicle attack as suspect appears in court
stories.summary: Independent MP Helen Haines had both legs amputated after a man allegedly struck her twice with his car outside her electoral office in Wangaratta; the accused appeared in court Wednesday. Lead with the outcome and the place: an MP attacked at the office where constituents walk in. The structural why is the exposure of Australian lawmakers' local offices amid rising threats to politicians.

stories.label: Eastern Libya parliament approves 2019 maritime deal with Turkiye
stories.summary: Libya's eastern parliament, long Haftar's base and hostile to Ankara, ratified the 2019 Turkey–Libya maritime boundary deal and lifted a 2020 boycott, so both rival Libyan governments now back it. Lead with the reversal: Turkey's former enemy in Libya just handed it a legal claim to gas blocks off North Africa that Greece and Cyprus dispute. Mechanism: eastern Mediterranean gas rights, and an EU dispute Ankara now argues from a united Libyan position.

stories.label: Rubio to push India on refining more crude
stories.summary: Rubio called India a 'refining superpower' and tours Reliance's Jamnagar refinery, the world's largest, to press India to refine more crude and ease fuel prices before the US midterms, while telling New Delhi that warmer US–Pakistan ties will not come at its expense. Lead with the ask: Washington wants India's refineries to absorb the Hormuz-driven fuel shock. Name Brent crude as the series.

stories.label: 89 CSOs demand release of Nigeria's investment treaty review, warn of risks to public funds
stories.summary: Eighty-nine civil society groups, Amnesty among them, demand Nigeria publish its review of bilateral investment treaties, warning that investor-state arbitration exposes public money to costly claims and blocks environmental rules on oil firms. Lead with the mechanism: ISDS lets foreign investors sue the state in private tribunals (Nigeria nearly lost $11bn in the P&ID case). Accountability: a review kept secret from the people whose funds are at stake.

stories.label: 永久保留缓存！OpenAI重磅更新，比DeepSeek还久？
stories.summary: OpenAI added a 12-hour prompt-cache option to its API for GPT-5.6 and later, but cache writes cost 2.5x the uncached input price, up from 1.25x, and the 12 hours is a billing window, not a guarantee of reuse. It lands a day after DeepSeek's open-source inference stack targeted three-day cache retention. Lead with the price doubling on writes; the reader is a developer paying per token. OpenAI also refunded credits to about 40,000 accounts.

stories.label: 骑手还没被替代，无人车们已经“内卷”麻了
stories.summary: China's driverless delivery-van makers (Meituan, Neolix and rivals) are already in a price war before they have replaced the couriers they were built to replace. Lead with the gap: involution among the robots while millions of riders still carry the load. Mechanism: subsidised fleets and financing ('grain before troops') competing for city permits, and who that leaves the riders with.

stories.label: Cleaning robotics startup Jingji Intelligent raises tens of millions of RMB in seed funding
stories.summary: A Shanghai cleaning-robot startup raised tens of millions of yuan a month after it was founded, from a robotics firm and a Shanghai state-linked industrial developer. Lead with the one-month gap: it shows how fast Chinese capital, much of it local-government money, now moves into embodied robotics. Mechanism: force-control manipulation for toilets, sinks and walls, the hard last mile of service robots.

stories.label: Superconductivity and ferroelectric orbital magnetism in semimetallic rhombohedral hexalayer graphene - Nature Physics
stories.summary: Six layers of carbon stacked in rhombohedral order superconduct and also carry a switchable orbital magnetism, two states physicists usually find to be enemies. Lead with the coexistence in plain material: no twisting, no exotic elements, just graphite stacked a particular way. Why it matters: a gate-switchable magnet that superconducts is a candidate route to new kinds of quantum devices.

stories.label: NATO to send planes and drones to Black Sea after attacks on shipping
stories.summary: NATO is sending more maritime patrol aircraft, radars and drones to the Black Sea after a run of deadly drone attacks on merchant shipping linked to Russia's war. Lead with who has been dying: crews of commercial ships, not navies. The mechanism: the Black Sea grain and trade corridor runs past Romania and Bulgaria, NATO members, so strikes on shipping pull the alliance closer to the war just as Washington pushes Kyiv toward a deal. Dateline Brussels.

stories.label: Makkah alliance binds partners to decade-long pact
stories.summary: Turkiye has sent the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan to parliament for ratification, the step that turns the signed pact into a binding ten-year commitment. Lead with what it obliges: joint defence among a NATO member, the Gulf's largest military spender and the Muslim world's only nuclear power. The structural why: as Houthi strikes reach the Gulf and US guarantees look conditional, Riyadh is building a Muslim-majority security bloc of its own. Dateline Ankara.

stories.label: Zelenskyy 'Thankful' To U.S. That Early Warning System 'Works Now'
stories.summary: New development since our Oslo story: Washington has restored the intelligence that warns Ukraine of incoming Russian missile and drone strikes, and Zelensky publicly thanked it, days after Trump struck a diesel deal with Putin and called for Zelensky to be replaced. Lead with the leverage: the warnings that get civilians into shelters were switched off and on as a bargaining chip. Next: Witkoff meets Putin. Dateline Kyiv.

stories.label: Built for boats, adrift on land: Bangladesh’s Bede community struggles with a fixed-address system
stories.summary: Bangladesh's Bede, a river-nomad people who lived on boats, are being pushed onto land by floods and river erosion, and a state built on fixed addresses cannot see them: no address means no national ID, and no ID means no healthcare, school places or vote. Lead with that chain. The structural why: climate displacement collides with paperwork designed for settled citizens, and the burden lands on one of the country's most marginalised Muslim communities. Dateline Dhaka.

stories.label: US food importer sues Trump over 50 percent tariffs on Canadian goods
stories.summary: A US food importer has sued at the Court of International Trade, arguing Trump used a century-old law to impose 50 percent tariffs on Canadian goods without Congress. Lead with who pays: the importer, and the American shoppers behind it, carry a tariff meant to punish Canada. The mechanism to explain: which statute the White House invoked, why it sidesteps Congress, and what a ruling would mean for the rest of the tariff programme. Dateline Washington.

stories.label: Japan shifting to wage-driven inflation phase, finance minister says
stories.summary: Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama says Japan is on the cusp of wage-driven inflation, while the government cuts the consumption tax and hands out payouts to cushion import costs driven up by the Iran war. Lead with the tension: Tokyo is easing prices for households with fiscal money just as it tells the Bank of Japan that inflation is becoming self-sustaining, which points to higher rates. Name the yen: a weak yen is what makes imported energy expensive. Dateline Tokyo.

stories.label: FBI says SafePay ransomware gang ‘among most active’ with more than 600 victims since 2024
stories.summary: The FBI, with cyber agencies in the UK and Germany, says the SafePay ransomware gang has hit more than 600 victims since 2024, including critical infrastructure. Lead with how mundane the entry is: guessed passwords, unpatched flaws and phishing, not exotic exploits. The point for a technical reader is what the joint advisory tells defenders to fix, and why a gang this prolific has gone unnamed until now. Dateline Washington.

stories.label: 腾讯联手蚂蚁，投了前豆包PC端负责人
stories.summary: Today AI, a Shanghai personal-assistant start-up founded only in March by Qi Junyuan, the former head of ByteDance's Doubao desktop app, has raised $200 million from Tencent, Ant Group, IDG, Sequoia China and Transsion. Lead with the speed and the backers: rival giants co-funding an ex-ByteDance product lead. The mechanism: the assistant reads a user's WeChat Work groups, meetings and documents to act before it is asked, and that always-on memory is the race China's labs and Meta and OpenAI are now running. Dateline Shanghai.

stories.label: 看面相断生死，AI居然真做到了？
stories.summary: An AI model that reads patients' faces flagged 122 people as at very high risk of death, and 64 of them died within 90 days. Lead with that number, then the questions a careful reader asks: which study, which patients, how it was validated, and how many deaths it missed. The stakes: a prognosis drawn from a photo could steer end-of-life care and insurance, and the article should say what the evidence does and does not show.

stories.label: A snow-jet bridging mechanism driving the Afro-Asian summer monsoon precipitation dipole - npj Climate and Atmospheric Science
stories.summary: A new study traces why rain in the African and Asian summer monsoons tends to move in opposite directions, wet in one when dry in the other, to snow cover upstream acting through the jet stream. Lead with who lives under it: farmers in the Sahel and South Asia whose harvests ride on these monsoons. The point: a physical link like this can make seasonal rainfall forecasts better for both regions at once.
